title: JudgeDefinition
description: WS-06. A versioned LLM judge (eval-harness.md section 4.2). Authored in the replicant-config repo under evals/judges/<name>.yaml, published by the eval-config CI into evals.judges (writer eval-worker via its admin API). Judge definitions are deliberately NOT part of Release Bundles: a judge measures bundles and must stay fixed across both arms of a comparison. digest = sha256(JCS(document)). A comparison is valid only if both arms were scored by the same judge (name, version, digest).

mode.description: pointwise: score one output against the rubric. pairwise: compare the two arms' outputs for the same task; both orders are scored and a preference counts only if consistent across orders.

jurors.description: One or more models. With two or more, the case score is the aggregation of juror scores, and juror disagreement is recorded. At least one juror must be from a different model family than every agent model in the bundles under comparison (self-preference guard), enforced at comparison start.

effort.description: Pinned explicitly because provider defaults differ by model (e.g. Claude Opus 5.5 defaults to medium).

use_batch.description: Reserved. The gateway has no batch path in v1 (eval-harness.md §3.4, XD-FIX-R2-063), so this must be false; a later gateway version may enable it.

prompt.description: Langfuse prompt pinned by version (never by label) plus its digest, verified at use exactly like bundle prompts.

inputs.description: What the judge sees. Candidate outputs are wrapped as untrusted data; the judge is never told which output is the baseline, the reference, or the candidate.

output.description: Structured output (JSON schema enforced through output_config.format). Each criterion is an atomic, separately scored property.

langfuse_score_config.description: Langfuse score config id the exported score validates against.

anchor_set.description: Name of the human-labelled anchor set in evals.anchor_sets.

known_negatives.description: Canary items injected into every judge batch; all must score at the scale minimum or the batch is invalid.
